subject: math
title: Change in Quantity: Find the Change and the Start
seo_title: Grade 2 Math: Change in Quantity Worksheets (Free, BC Curriculum, Answer Key)
standard_text: Change in quantity, using pictorial and symbolic representation
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on change in quantity for the BC curriculum: join and separate stories with pictures, writing number sentences like 28 + □ = 45, finding the change, finding the start and word problems to 100. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Start, change, end: find the part you do not know.
key_sub: Some come: add. Some go away: subtract. For 28 + □ = 45, count up from 28 to 45: 2 + 15 = 17. If the start is missing, work backward from the end. The start or end number is not the change.
body_html:
The idea: start, change, end

A change story has three parts. There is a start. Then there is a change: some come, or some go away. Then there is the end. Two parts are known. Find the one you do not know. Use a box □ for it.

What is missing?Some comeSome go away
The end28 + 17 = □52 − 22 = □
The change28 + □ = 4552 − □ = 30
The start□ + 17 = 45□ − 12 = 30

Join: some more come

Draw the start. Draw the ones that come. Count them all.

Separate: some go away

Draw the start. Cross out the ones that go away. Count the ones that are left.

Find the change

The start and the end are known. Count up from the start to the end. Jump to the next ten first.

Find the change

There were 52 people on the SkyTrain. At the next station, some people got off. Now there are 30. How many got off?

52 − □ = 30. Count up from 30 to 52: 30 + 20 = 50, 50 + 2 = 52. 20 + 2 = 22. Check: 52 − 22 = 30.

Answer: 22 people

Find the start: work backward

The start is missing. Go back from the end. If some came, take them away. If some went away, put them back.

Find the start

Liam had some hockey cards. He gave 12 to his friend. Now he has 30. How many did he have at the start?

□ − 12 = 30. Put back the 12 he gave away: 30 + 12 = 42. Check: 42 − 12 = 30.

Answer: 42 hockey cards

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the wrong operation: 28 + □ = 45, so 28 + 45 = 73The end is 45, so the change is less than 45. Count up from 28 to 45: 17.
Answering with the start amount: “28”28 is the start. The question asks for the change.
Answering with the end amount: □ + 17 = 45, so “45”45 is the end. Work backward: 45 − 17 = 28.
Not regrouping: 52 − 17 = 452 − 7 cannot be done. Regroup 1 ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Answer: 35.

Always check: put your answer in the box and read the story again.

faq.q: What does “change in quantity” mean in the BC Grade 2 math curriculum?
faq.a: It means an amount that goes up or down: some come or some go away. Grade 2 students show the change with pictures and with number sentences like 28 + □ = 45, using numbers to 100.

faq.q: How do you find the missing number in 28 + □ = 45?
faq.a: Count up from 28 to 45: 2 to get to 30, then 15 more, so □ = 17. You can also subtract: 45 − 28 = 17.

faq.q: How do you solve a story when the start is missing?
faq.a: Work backward from the end. If 17 came and now there are 45, take them away: 45 − 17 = 28. If 12 went away and 30 are left, put them back: 30 + 12 = 42.

faq.q: Why is change in quantity in the Patterning part of BC math?
faq.a: In BC, Patterning includes early algebra: seeing how an amount changes and using a symbol like □ for the unknown number. It builds toward solving equations in later grades.

sets.title: Join and separate stories with pictures

items.q: There were 5 people on the SkyTrain. At the next station, 4 more people got on. How many people are on the SkyTrain now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Count on from 5: 6, 7, 8, 9. 5 + 4 = 9. Answer: 9 people.

items.q: Ethan picked 9 apples at an orchard in the Okanagan. He gave 3 apples to his class. How many apples does Ethan have now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. 9 − 3 = 6. Answer: 6 apples.

items.q: There were 6 salmon in the creek. Then 5 more salmon swam in. How many salmon are in the creek now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. 6 + 5 = 11. Answer: 11 salmon.

items.q: At recess, 12 children were on the playground. Then 2 children went inside. How many children are on the playground now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. 12 − 2 = 10. Answer: 10 children.

items.q: There were 11 pucks in the bucket. The coach put in 3 more. How many pucks are in the bucket now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Count on from 11: 12, 13, 14. 11 + 3 = 14. Answer: 14 pucks.

items.q: Nadia had 18 hockey cards. She gave 4 cards to her friend. How many hockey cards does Nadia have now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. 18 − 4 = 14. Answer: 14 hockey cards.

items.q: Leah collected 11 pinecones in Stanley Park. Then she found 2 more. How many pinecones does Leah have now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Count on from 11: 12, 13. 11 + 2 = 13. Answer: 13 pinecones.
Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. 17 − 4 = 13. Answer: 13 shells.

items.q: Which number sentence matches the picture?
items.e: There are 9 apples. 4 more come. They are in the box. Some more come, so add: 9 + 4 = 13. 9 − 4 = 5 uses the wrong sign.
There are 15 shells. 6 are crossed out, so they go away. Subtract: 15 − 6 = 9. 15 + 6 = 21 uses the wrong sign.

items.q: The class library had 52 books. The teacher added 30 more. How many books are in the class library now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens. The ones stay the same. 52 + 30 = 82. Answer: 82 books.

items.q: There were 62 Canada geese on the pond. Then 20 geese flew away. How many geese are on the pond now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. 20 is 2 tens. Take away the tens. The ones stay the same. 62 − 20 = 42. Answer: 42 geese.

items.q: Simran read 42 pages of a book. The next day, she read 31 more pages. How many pages has Simran read now?
items.e: Some more came, so add. Tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Ones: 2 + 1 = 3. 70 + 3 = 73. Answer: 73 pages.

items.q: There were 32 bald eagles by the Fraser River. Then 2 eagles flew away. How many eagles are by the river now?
items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. Ones: 2 − 2 = 0. The tens stay the same. 32 − 2 = 30. Answer: 30 eagles.

items.e: Some more came, so add. Tens: 20 + 20 = 40. Ones: 9 + 5 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 40 + 14 = 54. Answer: 54 cars.

items.e: Some went away, so subtract. Do not add. Tens: 50 − 10 = 40. Ones: 7 − 6 = 1. 40 + 1 = 41. Answer: 41 stickers.

items.e: Some more came, so add. Tens: 30 + 10 = 40. Ones: 5 + 9 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 40 + 14 = 54. Answer: 54 children.

sets.title: Find the change: how many came or went?

items.q: What number goes in the box? 30 + □ = 50
items.e: Start at 30 and end at 50. Count up by tens from 30 to 50: 40, 50. That is 2 tens = 20. Check: 30 + 20 = 50.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 24 + □ = 54
items.e: Start at 24 and end at 54. Count up from 24: 24 + 6 = 30. 30 + 24 = 54. Add the jumps: 6 + 24 = 30. Check: 24 + 30 = 54.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 36 + □ = 40
items.e: Start at 36 and end at 40. Count up from 36 to 40: 37, 38, 39, 40. That is 4. Check: 36 + 4 = 40.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 28 + □ = 45
items.e: Start at 28 and end at 45. Count up from 28: 28 + 2 = 30. 30 + 15 = 45. Add the jumps: 2 + 15 = 17. Check: 28 + 17 = 45.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 60 − □ = 40
items.e: Jump back from 60 to 40. The jump is how far apart they are. Count up by tens from 40 to 60: 50, 60. That is 2 tens = 20. Check: 60 − 20 = 40.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 52 − □ = 30
items.e: Jump back from 52 to 30. The jump is how far apart they are. Count up from 30: 30 + 20 = 50. 50 + 2 = 52. Add the jumps: 20 + 2 = 22. Check: 52 − 22 = 30.

items.q: Mei had 26 stickers. She got some more. Now she has 41. Ryan says she got 67. What did Ryan do?
items.e: 26 + 41 = 67. But 67 is more than she has now. The change is the jump from 26 to 41: 26 + 4 = 30, 30 + 11 = 41, so she got 15. Ryan added 26 and 41.

items.q: There were 12 bald eagles by the Fraser River. Then some more eagles flew in. Now there are 42 eagles by the river. How many eagles flew in?
items.e: The change is missing: 12 + □ = 42. Count up from 12: 12 + 8 = 20. 20 + 22 = 42. Add the jumps: 8 + 22 = 30. Check: 12 + 30 = 42. Answer: 30 eagles.

items.q: There were 30 people on the SkyTrain. At the next station, some people got off. Now there are 8 people on the SkyTrain. How many people got off?
items.e: The change is missing: 30 − □ = 8. Find how far it is from 8 up to 30. Count up from 8: 8 + 2 = 10. 10 + 20 = 30. Add the jumps: 2 + 20 = 22. Check: 30 − 22 = 8. Answer: 22 people.

items.q: Lucas collected 13 pinecones in Stanley Park. Then he found some more. Now he has 27 pinecones. How many more pinecones did Lucas find?
items.e: The change is missing: 13 + □ = 27. Count up from 13: 13 + 7 = 20. 20 + 7 = 27. Add the jumps: 7 + 7 = 14. Check: 13 + 14 = 27. Answer: 14 pinecones.

items.q: Noah had 31 hockey cards. He gave some cards to his friend. Now he has 14 hockey cards. How many cards did Noah give away?
items.e: The change is missing: 31 − □ = 14. Find how far it is from 14 up to 31. Count up from 14: 14 + 6 = 20. 20 + 11 = 31. Add the jumps: 6 + 11 = 17. Check: 31 − 17 = 14. Answer: 17 hockey cards.

items.q: Wei had 18 shells from the beach. He found some more on Vancouver Island. Now he has 30 shells. How many shells did Wei find?
items.e: The change is missing: 18 + □ = 30. Count up from 18: 18 + 2 = 20. 20 + 10 = 30. Add the jumps: 2 + 10 = 12. Check: 18 + 12 = 30. Answer: 12 shells.

items.e: The change is missing: 32 + □ = 41. Count up from 32: 32 + 8 = 40. 40 + 1 = 41. Add the jumps: 8 + 1 = 9. Check: 32 + 9 = 41. Answer: 9 books.

items.e: Work backward from 50. 20 came, so take them away. 20 is 2 tens. Take away the tens. The ones stay the same. 50 − 20 = 30. Check: 30 + 20 = 50.

items.q: What number goes in the box? □ + 6 = 39

items.e: Work backward from 25. 10 went away, so put them back. 10 is 1 ten. Add the tens. The ones stay the same. 25 + 10 = 35. Check: 35 − 10 = 25.

items.q: What number goes in the box? □ + 17 = 45
items.e: Work backward from 45. 17 came, so take them away. 45 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Ones: 15 − 7 = 8. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. 45 − 17 = 28. Check: 28 + 17 = 45.
